title: VPC blueprint for air-gapped/private deployments - field notes
abstract: Field-oriented blueprint and quick-reference notes for delivering Redwood Private in air-gapped / highly restricted VPCs. Focused on offline artifact flow, deterministic Terraform behavior, staged upgrades, and pragmatic rollback patterns observed during recent pilots.
audience: SREs, deployment engineers, solutions engineers running customer on-prem/VPC installs (air-gapped or restricted egress). Useful for SEs prepping customer runbooks and field engineers executing first installs.
prerequisites:
- Customer provides: CIDR allocation for control plane and worker subnets, physical connectivity plan (cross-connect, VPN, or transfer medium), KMS/HSM access, and hardware inventory (GPU sku + disks).
- Build infra: an airgap provisioning host (ubuntu 22.04), a local package registry (harbor/artifactory), container images and node OS images exported as tarballs, and signed TLS certs for control plane endpoints.
- Credentials: ephemeral deployment service account with restricted scope, a rotating SSH keypair for bastion, and offline token for license/activation if required.
high_level_architecture: 1) Customer VPC segmented into: management (bastion/provisioning), control-plane (control plane APIs, registry mirror), worker-pool(s) (GPU hosts), and optional NFS/Artifact storage. 2) All egress is blocked by default; selective egress only for provisioning host to Redwood support IPs when allowed. 3) Local artifact registry + internal DNS for image resolution. 4) Lightweight edge-proxy (squid or nginx) for controlled package push/pull. 5) Optional inter-site replication for HA across co-lo racks.
stepwise_deployment_plan: 1) Preflight (remote): collect hardware, internal peering diagram, routing/firewall ACLs, MTU, and L3/L4 rules. 2) Build offline bundle in staging: docker images (inference runtime, sidecars), deb/rpm packages, tf state backend bootstrap objects (S3-compatible minio) and IaC templates. 3) Validate artifacts in an isolated test network (lab mirror of customer CIDR). 4) Provision control-plane subnets and internal load balancers via Terraform with `-parallelism=10` and remote state locked. 5) Bootstrap local registry and push images; update internal DNS records. 6) Apply node pools (GPU workers) with node labels and taints for canary. 7) Deploy control-plane services, enable health-checks, and run smoke tests. 8) Promote canary worker group to full by rotating node pools with rolling drain. 9) Run post-deploy validation (end-to-end perf + quality eval sets).
terraform_module_notes:
- Provider locking: pin provider versions in modules to avoid drift between engineer laptops and CI (example: provider registry.terraform.io/hashicorp/aws ~> 4.0).
- Remote state: prefer S3-compatible (minio) in airgap; initialize backend with `terraform init -reconfigure` after registry bootstrap.
- Idempotency caveat: dynamic block for secondary ENIs caused diffs on hosts with mixed MTUs; avoid computed host-level attrs where possible.
- Module outputs: expose internal lb dns, subnet ids, and bootstrap keys explicitly (do not rely on implicit planning outputs).
- Workaround: some customers' infra restricts IMDS calls; add optional flag `disable_imds_discovery` to aws-node module to rely on passed instance metadata.
- Versioning: adopt a module compatibility matrix file in repo root (module -> tested provider versions -> notes).
upgrade_and_rollback_strategy:
- Strategy: staged (canary -> small cohort -> full). For control-plane upgrades prefer blue/green when change is invasive (DB schema), otherwise rolling restart.
- Upgrade steps: snapshot DB and etcd, export artifact bundle for rollback, deploy canary control-plane instances with new image tag, verify health & metrics for 30m, gradually shift traffic via internal LB weights.
- Rollback: if canary fails, revert LB weights to old control-plane and redeploy old images to canary nodes, then run `terraform apply` with previous tfstate snapshot. For stateful DB migrations include a reversible migration pattern (versioned migration script + feature-flag toggle).
- Quick commands (field): `kubectl cordon <node> && kubectl drain <node> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data` for draining; `aws s3 cp s3://backup/state.tfstate ./state.tfstate` to fetch backup in airgap proxies that replicate S3.
validation_and_smoke_tests: KV cache sanity: run sample workload that warms and validates cache hit/miss curves
Tokenized throughput: run 3x small batch generation (length 512) and observe p50/p95 under budget
End-to-end consistency: run canonical prompt set and diff against baseline outputs (allow minor float variance)
Failure injection: kill one control-plane pod and assert automatic failover within SLO
troubleshooting_cheatsheet:
- Image pull failures: confirm registry cert chain and that images were pushed with `docker save|load` test in lab.
- Unexpected TF diffs: run `terraform plan -out=tfplan.bin` and inspect provider version in `.terraform.lock.hcl`. If computed attributes differ, add lifecycle ignore_changes to that attribute.
- DNS resolution issues: check that registrar was updated on provisioning host and that CoreDNS configmap includes forward stub for internal-registry.
- Node network flaps: check MTU mismatch between switch and host; common sign is fragmentation errors in dmesg.
- TLS handshake failures: verify SANs in customer-provided certs; internal-hostnames must match LB DNS names.
- Slow cold-starts: verify KV cache warm path and container start probe times; tune readiness/liveness probes accordingly.
unresolved_questions: Do we require signed license tokens for every customer airgap bundle or a single signed bundle per account?
What is minimum set of outbound IPs customers are willing to white-list for support telemetry?
Should we formalize an offline package format (.rwdbundle) that our CLI recognizes for deterministic installs?
